headline: Heard presentation and public comment on proposed $4,750,000 purchase of Chippanee Golf Course; no vote taken.
summary: The Mayor and Parks and Recreation Superintendent presented information on the budget, capital projects, taxes, and golf course management models for a possible purchase of Chippanee Golf Course. Residents spoke for and against the purchase, and several others sent emails or calls in favor. The minutes record no vote on the purchase.
plain_text:
439 
SEPTEMBER 3, 2026 
The special meeting of the City Council was held on Thursday, September 3, 2026 in the City 
Hall Council Chambers, 111 North Main Street at 6:30 p.m. Present: Mayor Zoppo-Sassu; Council 
Members Dickau, Hahn, Rosengren, Seymour, and Tyler.  Present by videoconference:  Council 
Member Kelley. 
  
1. CALL TO ORDER 
  
2. INFORMATIONAL PRESENTATION 
  
 Mayor Zoppo-Sassu presented information on the budget, capital projects, the Plan of 
Conservation and Development Goals, the estimated impact on taxes if Chippanee were to be 
purchased and maintained as a municipal golf course, and the investigative steps taken as part of the 
due diligence process.  The proposed purchase price of $4,750,000 includes all the acreage, the Club 
House, fixtures, furniture, and equipment.   
 
 Parks and Recreation Superintendent Josh Medeiros explained that his role thus far has been 
to assess potential benefits of the acquisition and to research other municipalities that are currently 
managing public golf courses.  He presented his findings on governance structure, management 
models, and budget structure of these golf courses.  He also spoke of the process that would happen 
should the City Council vote to move forward with the acquisition. 
 
 A printed version of the PowerPoint presentation is on file in the Town Clerk’s Office. 
  
3. PUBLIC PARTICIPATION  
 
 The following people spoke in opposition to purchasing Chippanee Golf Course: 
- Robert Boudreau, 41 Broadview St. – Concerned about operating model, drainage issues, 
and the long-term impact on taxes. 
- Michael LaMothe, 186 Dino Rd. – Concerned about Chippanee’s financials, would like 
to see the tax returns, and suggested signed and notarized conflict of interest statements 
from all involved. 
 
The following people spoke in favor of purchasing Chippanee Golf Course for various 
reasons including, but not limited to, the preservation of open space, a public golf course 
being a draw to the area, and maintaining the history of a “treasure” in town:  “Mickey” 
Marvin Goldwasser, 171 Diane Ln.;  James Collins, 145 Fox Den Rd.;  William Fontaine, 51 
Ashover Ln.;  Deborah Schur, 6 Pilgrim Rd.;  Nicole Elliott, Marsh Rd.;  Mary Ann Sirois, 
362 Shrub Rd.;  Robert Marsh, 68 Medford St.;  Anthony Lorenzetti, 150 Pinnacle Rd.;  
Timothy Gamache, 1389 Stafford Ave.;  Paul Krolikowski, 148 Crown St.;  Stephen Repass, 
address unknown;  Brian Kelly, 251 Pennwood Pl.;  Daniel Delcegno, 906 Hill St.;  Denise 
Davis, 371 Emmett St.;  and Thomas Selnau, 9 Mano Ln. 
 
Jane Murdock, 400 Shrub Rd. – Asked if there would be an operating budget before the vote 
and if the public would have another opportunity to speak before a vote would be taken.  She 
did not voice her opinion. 
 
Mathew Biadun, 53 Buff Rd. – Submitted a letter expressing concern over the possibility of 
burdening the city with something it cannot afford to maintain.
440 
SEPTEMBER 3, 2026 
The Mayor’s Office received emails and/or phone calls in favor of purchasing Chippanee 
Golf Course from the following people who were unable to attend the meeting:  Paul Wibley, 
Frank Stawski, Andrea Adams, Mark Moriarty, Robert Douglas, Hal Kilby, and Keith 
Odume.    
 
  
4. ADJOURNMENT 
 
At 7:59 p.m., on motion of Council Member Seymour and seconded by Council Member 
Rosengren, it was unanimously voted:  To adjourn.

                  Erica Cabiya 
       Town & City Clerk
